human_tolerance.notes: Authored. Wikipedia says crevices in buildings or walls are sometimes used for nesting; no source gives a garden or light tolerance.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Typical European clutch laid March to June (Wikipedia). Not GB-specific.

vocalizations.description: Male song: srrih notes, then twittering, a descending ripple and a falling-then-rising whistle (Wikipedia).

taxonomy.note: Genus Certhia, family Certhiidae, ACCEPTED at species rank in GBIF 2487603 (checked 2026-11-01).

external.note: GBIF 2487603 checked at GBIF species endpoint (ACCEPTED, SPECIES). iNaturalist 7450 (active, species) via Wikidata P3151, cross-checked against iNaturalist taxa API on 2026-11-01.

common_names.note: Article title; Wikidata English label 'Eurasian Treecreeper'.

range.note: Partial list. Wikipedia says the species breeds in temperate woodland across the Palearctic from Ireland to Japan, and names the British Isles. Other countries are NOT yet supported by a permissive source; the list is a known gap.

traits.mass_kg.note: BodyMass-Value 9 g, Dunning08, species-level. Wikipedia gives only the range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The typical lifespan is two years' (Breeding). Maximum 8 years 10 months is NOT used. The ADW average life expectancy of 2 years matches but is CC BY-NC-SA and is not cited.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Creeps and hops up trunks (Habits); flight by migrants and fleeing (Distribution, Habits). Poor-flier wording is from ADW (NC) and is not cited.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in tree crevices or behind bark flakes (Breeding).

traits.perching.note: Authored: no source says it perches on branches; it creeps on trunks. Set false.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 60, Diet-Seed 40. Wikipedia describes invertebrates as the primary diet and conifer seeds only as a colder-months addition, so the seed share is in tension with the text. Reviewer decision needed.

traits.social.note: Solitary in winter (Habits). Breeding pair structure not stated.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0. Foraging described on trunks in daylight (Feeding).

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement: small cryptic woodland bird, easily overlooked (Habits).

habitat.use.note: ForStrat-ground 40; understory 30 plus midhigh 30 mapped to arboreal 60.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrates from trunks (Feeding); seed weight from EltonTraits Diet-Seed.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts in a sheltered crevice in cold weather (Habits); tag choice authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Authored. Wikipedia says buildings or walls are sometimes used for nesting.

seasonal.strategy.note: Scoped to GB. Wikipedia: non-migratory in the milder west and south of the breeding range, while northern birds move south in winter. A species-wide PartialMigration needs a winter_fraction that no source gives, so GB is recorded as ActiveYearRound. Known simplification; reviewer decision needed.

seasonal.phases.note: Typical clutch March to June in Europe (Breeding). Not GB-specific.

activity.GB.note: Filled by tools/fetch_activity.py. See the activity section below.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Eggs and breeding from age one year (Breeding). Juvenile stage listed without a duration, which no source gives.

behavior.note: Species-local program bt-treecreeper-trunk-v1 (behavior.json). Climb gait for foraging on trunks (Feeding, Habits), flight for fleeing, March to June nest window (Breeding). Derived from the shared bt-perching-songbird-v1 with the food gait changed from hop to climb. Climb has no built-in pose, so trunk creeping renders with the idle pose.

look.note: Brown upperparts, whitish underparts, curved bill, long stiff tail (Description). Palette and proportions authored.

traits.body_plan.note: Bird class facts; the article describes a feathered, flying passerine.
